Name: Tibet Trek
Description: A week on the Tibetan plateau: the Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple and Sera Monastery in Lhasa, then sacred lakes, a glacier and the north face of Everest. Travel is by private vehicle with short, easy walks; the itinerary is tentative and subject to permit approval.
Price includes: Hotels approved for foreign visitors, Tibet Travel Permit, licensed guide and transportation. Excludes flights to and from Lhasa and a Chinese visa if you need one.
Destination blurb: Pilgrims circling the Jokhang at dawn, monks debating in Sera's courtyard, and the north face of Everest from passes above 17,000 ft. Foreign visitors can only travel in Tibet with a permit, a licensed agency and a guide, which is why this is a group trip.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Lhasa and rest (12,000 ft).
Day 2: Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple and Sera Monastery; dinner with a local family.
Day 3: Yamdrok-tso lake, Karo La glacier and Manla Reservoir; night in Shigatse.
Day 4: Tashilhunpo Monastery, then over Gyatso La (17,260 ft) to Tingri.
Day 5: Gawu La, the Everest viewing area and Rongbuk Monastery; back to Tingri.
Day 6: Drive back to Lhasa (8-10 hours).
Day 7: Fly home.

Name: Brazil Trek: Amazon and Rio
Description: Four days at a jungle lodge near Manaus, with jungle walks, pink river dolphins and visits to Indigenous and riverside communities, then four days in Rio with Christ the Redeemer, the Dois Irmãos hike and a farewell boat party.
Price includes: Amazon jungle lodge (3 nights, all meals and soft drinks), guided activities, Manaus-Rio flight, 4 nights at the Sheraton Grand Rio with breakfast, included tours and the boat party, transfers and an eSIM. Excludes international flights, visa and mandatory travel insurance. Prices are for a shared triple room in the Amazon and a double room in Rio.
Destination blurb: Two sides of Brazil in one week: the world's largest rainforest from a jungle lodge alongside local communities, then Rio's beaches, samba and landmarks. Run by Parrot Trips, with a staff member with the group at all times.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Manaus, transfer to the jungle lodge, welcome dinner and a night caiman-spotting boat ride.
Day 2: Guided jungle walk (survival skills, wildlife, native plants), lunch at the lodge, piranha fishing.
Day 3: Pink river dolphins, the Kubeua Indigenous community, and a riverside family's açaí harvest and cassava flour making.
Day 4: Sunrise on the river, check-out, flight to Rio, free evening.
Day 5: Train up Corcovado to Christ the Redeemer, the Selarón steps, then street fair and live samba at Rua do Senado.
Day 6: Dois Irmãos hike and a favela visit with a local guide.
Day 7: All-inclusive boat party on Guanabara Bay.
Day 8: Check-out and departure.

Name: Tanzania Trek
Description: Safari and Zanzibar beaches: three days of game drives in Tarangire, Ndutu and the Ngorongoro Crater, then Zanzibar with a dhow cruise, snorkeling at Mnemba Atoll and a spice tour in Stone Town.
Price includes: Accommodation, meals, domestic flights and activities. Excludes international flights, visas, private transfers for groups under 5, scuba diving, alcohol and tips (about $50 for the safari).
Destination blurb: Baobabs and elephant herds in Tarangire, the Big Five in the world's largest intact volcanic caldera, and a visit with the Hadzabe, one of Tanzania's oldest communities. Then fly to Zanzibar for turquoise water, dolphins and Stone Town's spice markets.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive at Kilimanjaro airport, transfer to Arusha, group dinner.
Day 2: Full-day safari in Tarangire National Park; night in Karatu.
Day 3: Full-day game drive in Ndutu, in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area.
Day 4: Game drive in the Ngorongoro Crater.
Day 5: Visit the Hadzabe tribe or a local artisan market, fly to Zanzibar, dinner in Stone Town, then on to Kendwa.
Day 6: Free morning; sunset dhow cruise.
Day 7: Snorkeling or diving at Mnemba Atoll; rest of the day free.
Day 8: Spice tour, farewell lunch, Stone Town, evening flight home.

Name: Patagonia: W Trek
Description: Five days hiking the W Trek in Torres del Paine National Park, about 7-14 miles a day, with mountain guides, all camping gear and meals on the trail. Runs as two groups of 12.
Price includes: Travel insurance, airport/hotel/park transfers, mountain guides, park entrance fees, all camping and refugio gear (tents, sleeping bags and pads), all meals on the trek, 2 hotel nights in Puerto Natales (before and after the trek) and a celebration barbecue. Excludes flights.
Destination blurb: Granite towers, glaciers and turquoise lakes at the bottom of South America. Torres del Paine is one of the great trekking parks in the world, and park permit rules mean tickets need final names within 30 days of registering. Open to Wharton Outdoors Club members.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Puerto Natales; hotel night.
Days 2-6: Hike the W Trek in Torres del Paine (about 7-14 miles a day), camping and staying in refugios.
Day 7: Back in Puerto Natales after a hotel night; departure.
Price 1 note: $1,000 deposit due by midnight on the day you get a spot.

Name: Patagonia: O Trek
Description: The full O loop around Torres del Paine: seven hiking days of about 7-14 miles each, with mountain guides, all camping gear and meals on the trail. The more demanding of the two Patagonia treks, run as a single group.
Price includes: Travel insurance, airport/hotel/park transfers, mountain guides, park entrance fees, all camping and refugio gear (tents, sleeping bags and pads), all meals on the trek, 2 hotel nights in Puerto Natales (before and after the trek) and a celebration barbecue. Excludes flights.
Destination blurb: Granite towers, glaciers and turquoise lakes at the bottom of South America. Torres del Paine is one of the great trekking parks in the world, and park permit rules mean tickets need final names within 30 days of registering. Open to Wharton Outdoors Club members.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Puerto Natales; hotel night.
Days 2-8: Hike the O loop in Torres del Paine (about 7-14 miles a day), camping and staying in refugios.
Day 9: Back in Puerto Natales after a hotel night; departure.
Price 1 note: $1,000 deposit due by midnight on the day you get a spot.

Name: Dogsledding in Kiruna (Wave 1)
Description: Two full days driving husky teams through the wilderness around Kiruna, returning each evening to a wilderness lodge for sauna and dinner, with chances to see the Northern Lights.
Price includes: Winter clothing (jackets, trousers, overalls, boots and gloves) and meals. Excludes flights.
Destination blurb: Swedish Lapland in the depths of winter: frozen lakes, snowy forest, saunas at a wilderness lodge and a good chance of the Northern Lights, cloud cover permitting. No experience needed; the first afternoon is spent getting to know the huskies.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Kiruna; short sledding tour to meet the huskies.
Day 2: Full day of sledding through forest and over frozen lakes; evening at the Wilderness Lodge.
Day 3: Another full day of sledding; sauna and relaxing at the lodge.
Day 4: Departure.
Price 1 note: Paid in full by midnight on the day you register.

Name: Dogsledding in Kiruna (Wave 2)
Description: The January run of the Kiruna trip: two full days driving husky teams through forest and over frozen lakes, evenings at a wilderness lodge, and chances to see the Northern Lights.
Price includes: Winter clothing (jackets, trousers, overalls, boots and gloves) and meals. Excludes flights.
Destination blurb: Swedish Lapland in the depths of winter: frozen lakes, snowy forest, saunas at a wilderness lodge and a good chance of the Northern Lights, cloud cover permitting. No experience needed; the first afternoon is spent getting to know the huskies.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Kiruna; short sledding tour to meet the huskies.
Day 2: Full day of sledding through forest and over frozen lakes; evening at the Wilderness Lodge.
Day 3: Another full day of sledding; sauna and relaxing at the lodge.
Day 4: Departure.

Name: Antarctica Expedition
Cities: Ushuaia; South Shetland Islands; Antarctic Peninsula
Description: A Wharton/Penn group voyage from Ushuaia across the Drake Passage to the South Shetlands and the Antarctic Peninsula aboard the Discoverer, a 140-guest expedition ship. Up to six hours a day off the ship: landings among penguins, zodiac cruises, kayaking, a night camping on the ice and the polar plunge.
Price includes: Pre-departure hotel night in Ushuaia, all meals on board, house drinks with lunch and dinner, an expedition parka to keep and boots to borrow, off-ship excursions, kayaking and camping, and 24/7 travel support. Excludes flights to Ushuaia.
Destination blurb: Your seventh continent: penguin colonies, whales and seals, and icebergs seen from a kayak. A small ship with one guide for every seven guests means more time ashore, plus citizen science projects along the way.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Ushuaia; pre-departure hotel night.
Day 2: Board the Discoverer and sail into the Drake Passage.
Middle days: South Shetland Islands and the Antarctic Peninsula, with landings, zodiac cruises, kayaking, an overnight camp and the polar plunge.
Final days: Cross the Drake Passage back to Ushuaia.
Price 1 note: About $11.8K depending on cabin; 25% deposit to reserve a spot.

Name: Scuba Diving in Cozumel
Description: Six nights of Caribbean diving on Cozumel's Palancar and Santa Rosa walls. Beginners get PADI Open Water certified in the first three days; certified divers do two-tank boat dives every day, with optional extra and night dives. Mornings or afternoons off for the beach and the island. Two prices: $1,350 for beginners, including the PADI Open Water course, or $1,200 for certified divers (proof of PADI Open Water or equivalent required).
Price includes: Six nights at Hotel Plaza in downtown San Miguel with breakfast (two sharing), diving with Blue Note Scuba (a PADI 5 Star centre), all gear and computer rental, marine park fees and PADI eLearning. Excludes flights, dive insurance, meals, drinks, tips and airport transfers.
Destination blurb: Some of the clearest water in the world, with turtles and eagle rays along the walls. Led by a PADI Master Scuba Diver Trainer with more than 2,500 dives; first-timers are welcome, and anyone rusty starts with a refresher dive.
Itinerary:
Day 1 (Sun): Arrive in Cozumel and check in.
Days 2-4 (Mon-Wed): Beginners do the PADI Open Water course, certified by Wednesday lunch; certified divers do two-tank boat dives.
Days 5-6 (Thu-Fri): Reef boat dives for everyone.
Day 7 (Sat): Departure.
Every day: alternate mornings or afternoons off.

Name: Guatemala: Acatenango and Lake Atitlán
Description: Six days in Guatemala built around an overnight climb of Acatenango, camping across from the erupting Fuego volcano, then a sunrise summit at 13,044 ft. Rated hard: about 5,100 ft of steep, non-technical climbing with loose ash near the top and below-freezing temperatures before dawn. Starts in Antigua and ends at Lake Atitlán.
Destination blurb: One of the few places on earth where you can sleep across from an active eruption. Colonial Antigua and the volcano-ringed Lake Atitlán bookend the climb.
Itinerary:
Day 1 (Wed 12/16): Arrive and check in.
Day 2 (Thu 12/17): Coffee tour or Antigua walking tour.
Day 3 (Fri 12/18): Hike to high camp (12,300 ft) and watch Fuego erupt.
Day 4 (Sat 12/19): Summit at sunrise, descend to Antigua.
Day 5 (Sun 12/20): Lake Atitlán activity.
Day 6 (Mon 12/21): Lake Atitlán, departure.
Price 1 note: Pay in full within 24 hours of getting a spot.

Name: Kilimanjaro: Lemosho Route
Description: A seven-day guided climb of Kilimanjaro on the Lemosho Route, through five climate zones from rainforest to arctic summit, with a sunrise push to Uhuru Peak at 19,341 ft. Nights are spent camping with a full mountain crew of guides and porters.
Price includes: Guided 7-day trek with full mountain crew, tents, hot meals and porters. Excludes flights, extra hotel nights and tips.
Destination blurb: The highest point in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world. The Lemosho Route is one of the quieter, more scenic ways up, and its slower pace helps with acclimatisation.
Itinerary:
Day 1: Arrive in Tanzania.
Days 2-8: Climb the Lemosho Route, camping each night, with a sunrise summit of Uhuru Peak.
Day 9: Departure.
See the proposed itinerary link for the day-by-day plan.
Price 1 note: $1,000 deposit at signup, invoiced by the agency.

Name: Caucasus Cat and Backcountry Skiing
Description: Six days of untouched powder in Bakhmaro, Georgia: about four days of unlimited cat skiing and two days of guided ski touring, with no lifts and no crowds. For very experienced off-piste skiers with avalanche training and touring experience.
Price includes: Four days of unlimited cat skiing, two days of guided ski touring, airport transfer to Bakhmaro, six hotel nights and meals. Touring skis, skins, beacon, shovel and probe can be rented from the guides. Excludes flights.
Destination blurb: Bakhmaro gets around 18 ft of snow a year, one of the deepest accessible snowpacks anywhere. Guided by The Alpine Project, a local IFMGA/GMGA-certified company. No avalanche training yet? Sign up for WOC's Backcountry Skills Clinic at US Ski in Jackson.
Itinerary:
Day 1 (3/6): Arrive in Tbilisi and transfer to Bakhmaro.
Days 2-7 (3/7-3/12): Cat skiing (unlimited laps, aiming for about 8 a day or 13,000 vertical ft) or ski touring.
Day 8 (3/13): Half-day of skiing, then transfer back to Tbilisi.
Price 1 note: Interest form only for now; final price to be confirmed.

Name: Ghana Trek
Description: New Year's in Accra with the Wharton African Students Association: a city tour, drumming and batik with a local family, a day trip to Kakum National Park's canopy walk and Elmina Castle, and a rooftop New Year's Eve dinner, with free days to explore.
Price includes: 6 nights at the ESP Hotel in Accra, daily breakfast, 3 lunches and 2 dinners, airport arrival transfers, air-conditioned bus for itinerary activities, entry to all listed sites, travel hosts and local guides, and a welcome bag. Excludes international flights, travel insurance, visa, vaccinations, other meals and drinks, optional activities and tips.
Destination blurb: Markets, music and history in West Africa's liveliest capital, plus the rainforest and the coast's slave-trade castles. Run by Enroute54 Africa Travel for a group of 10 to 20. U.S. passport holders need a visa, and a yellow fever certificate is required on arrival.
Itinerary:
Day 1 (Dec 27): Arrive at Accra airport (ACC), transfer to the hotel, welcome dinner at 7 PM.
Day 2: City tour of Makola Market, Jamestown, the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial and Black Star Square; drumming class, Arts Centre shopping and lunch. Optional night at Afrofuture.
Day 3: Day with a local family: batik, Adinkra symbols, cooking and a traditional lunch. Optional Afrofuture day 2.
Day 4: Central Region day trip: hike and canopy walk in Kakum National Park, Elmina Castle, beachside lunch.
Day 5 (Dec 31): Free day; New Year's Eve dinner at Skybar. Optional party at Polo Beach Club with fireworks.
Day 6 (Jan 1): Free day with optional activities.
Day 7 (Jan 2): Last-minute shopping, airport transfer and departure.

Name: India GIP
Description: A Global Immersion Program on the economic, cultural and geopolitical forces shaping India, with company visits and cultural activities in New Delhi, Agra and Mumbai. Pre-departure lectures are on campus, on Tuesdays in Q2.
Price includes: Hotels and breakfasts, activities and excursions, opening and closing dinners, travel between cities and group transport, guides and their tips. Excludes flights to and from India, visas, other meals and airport transfers.
Itinerary:
Dec 27 – Jan 1: New Delhi (The Imperial). Programming starts the morning of Dec 28.
Jan 1 – 6: Mumbai (Trident, Nariman Point). Programming ends the evening of Jan 5.
Agra is also on the itinerary.
Pre-departure lectures: Tuesdays in Q2, 5:15–6:45pm (Oct 27, Nov 3, Nov 10, Nov 17, Dec 1).

Name: Japan GIP
Description: A Global Immersion Program on the economic, cultural and geopolitical forces shaping Japan, in Tokyo and Kyoto, including attendance at the Wharton Global Forum. Pre-departure lectures are virtual, on Tuesdays in Q3.
Price includes: Hotels, all breakfasts and some lunches and dinners, group transport (buses, trains), cultural activities and on-location course costs. Excludes flights to and from Japan, visas, taxis, other meals and incidentals.
Itinerary:
Mar 7 – 9: Tokyo (Shibuya Excel Hotel Tokyu). Arrive by the afternoon of Mar 7 for the opening dinner.
Mar 9 – 11: Kyoto (DoubleTree by Hilton Kyoto Station).
Mar 11 – 14: Tokyo (Hotel New Otani). Programming ends the evening of Mar 13.
Pre-departure sessions (virtual): Tuesdays in Q3, 5:15–6:45pm ET (Jan 26 orientation; Feb 2, 9 and 16 lectures; Feb 23 pre-departure session).

Name: Argentina GIP
Description: Reform, Risk, and Opportunity: a Global Immersion Program on how Argentina's sweeping reforms are reshaping its business environment, with company visits in e-commerce, fintech, energy and technology in Buenos Aires and Bariloche (Patagonia).
Price includes: Hotels, all breakfasts and some lunches and dinners, group transport (buses, flights), cultural activities including a half-day at an estancia outside Buenos Aires and a full day in Bariloche, and on-location course costs. Excludes flights to and from Argentina, visas, taxis, other meals and incidentals.
Destination blurb: Argentina is in a period of profound political, economic and social change. Move between Buenos Aires, its political and financial center, and Bariloche in Patagonia, a hub of technology and regional development, to see how reform is reshaping investment and strategy.
Itinerary:
Depart the evening of Fri, Mar 5 for a Sat, Mar 6 arrival.
Mar 6 – 10: Buenos Aires (Recoleta Grand Hotel). Programming starts the evening of Mar 6.
Mar 10 – 13: Bariloche, Patagonia (NH Bariloche Edelweiss). Programming ends the evening of Mar 12.
Pre-departure lectures: Tuesdays in Q3, 5:15–6:45pm (Jan 26; Feb 2, 9, 16 and 23).
Confirm all spring exam dates before committing.

Name: Kenya GIP
Description: A Global Immersion Program on the economic, cultural and geopolitical forces shaping Kenya, from Nairobi to the coast at Mombasa. Pre-departure lectures are on campus, on Tuesdays in Q4.
Itinerary:
May 11 – 16: Nairobi (Hyatt Place Nairobi Westlands). Programming starts the morning of May 12.
May 16 – 20: Mombasa (Serena Beach Resort & Spa). Programming ends the evening of May 19.
Pre-departure lectures: Tuesdays in Q4, 5:15–6:45pm (Mar 23, Mar 30, Apr 6, Apr 13, Apr 20).
Price 1 note: Double and single room fees are still TBD.
